data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism asserts a 'strategic choice to act on the theory that has withstood the most severe attempts at refutation, thereby maximizing our proximity to truth (verisimilitude) without claiming probability.' The word 'thereby' does all the logical work but is unsupported. There are only two ways to read the connection between surviving severe tests and 'maximizing proximity to truth': (1) as a stipulative definition, where 'verisimilitude' is merely renamed 'having survived severe tests' — in which case the claim is trivially true but philosophically empty, since it no longer means truth-likeness at all and provides no rational basis for preference over coin-flipping; or (2) as a substantive empirical assertion that surviving severe tests actually correlates with being closer to the truth — which is precisely the inductive inference Popper's framework forbids. The target cannot have it both ways: if the link is definitional, the defense is vacuous; if it is substantive, it smuggles in induction through the back door. This is distinct from the already-raised Tichý/Miller objection, which concerns the formal definability of verisimilitude. This objection concerns the logical bridge between corroboration and verisimilitude even if verisimilitude were perfectly definable.
